# AshCloak

AshCloak is an [Ash](https://hexdocs.pm/ash) extension to seamlessly encrypt and decrypt attributes of your resources.

Encrypting attributes ensures that sensitive fields are not stored in the clear in your data layer.

AshCloak can be used with any Ash data layer.

It's recommended to use [Cloak](https://github.com/danielberkompas/cloak) as a vault implementation but you could also build your own.

## Tutorials

# AshCloak

Source: https://ash-cloak.hexdocs.pm/AshCloak.md

# `AshCloak`
[🔗](https://github.com/ash-project/ash_cloak/blob/v0.3.1/lib/ash_cloak.ex#L5)

An extension for encrypting attributes of a resource.

See the getting started guide for more information.

# `cloak`
*macro* 

# `encrypt_and_set`

Encrypts and writes to an encrypted attribute.

If the changeset is pending (i.e not currently running the action), then it is added as a before_action hook.
Otherwise, it is run immediately

Raises AshCloak.Errors.NoSuchEncryptedAttribute if the attribute is not configured for encryption.

[🔗](https://github.com/ash-project/ash_cloak/blob/v0.3.1/lib/ash_cloak/changes/encrypt.ex#L5)

Takes an argument, and encrypts it into an attribute called `encrypted_{attribute}`

# AshCloak.Info

Source: https://ash-cloak.hexdocs.pm/AshCloak.Info.md

# `AshCloak.Info`
[🔗](https://github.com/ash-project/ash_cloak/blob/v0.3.1/lib/ash_cloak/info.ex#L5)

Introspection functions for the `AshCloak` extension.

# `cloak_attributes`

```elixir
@spec cloak_attributes(dsl_or_extended :: module() | map()) ::
  {:ok, [atom()]} | :error
```

The attribute or attributes to encrypt. The attribute will be renamed to `encrypted_{attribute}`, and a calculation with the same name will be added.

# `cloak_attributes!`

```elixir
@spec cloak_attributes!(dsl_or_extended :: module() | map()) :: [atom()] | no_return()
```

The attribute or attributes to encrypt. The attribute will be renamed to `encrypted_{attribute}`, and a calculation with the same name will be added.

# `cloak_decrypt_by_default`

```elixir
@spec cloak_decrypt_by_default(dsl_or_extended :: module() | map()) ::
  {:ok, [atom()]} | :error
```

A list of attributes that should be decrypted (their calculation should be loaded) by default.

# `cloak_decrypt_by_default!`

```elixir
@spec cloak_decrypt_by_default!(dsl_or_extended :: module() | map()) ::
  [atom()] | no_return()
```

A list of attributes that should be decrypted (their calculation should be loaded) by default.

# `cloak_on_decrypt`

```elixir
@spec cloak_on_decrypt(dsl_or_extended :: module() | map()) ::
  {:ok, (any(), any(), any(), any() -&gt; any()) | mfa()} | :error
```

A function to call when decrypting any value. Takes the resource, field, records, and calculation context. Must return `:ok` or `{:error, error}`

# `cloak_on_decrypt!`

```elixir
@spec cloak_on_decrypt!(dsl_or_extended :: module() | map()) ::
  ((any(), any(), any(), any() -&gt; any()) | mfa()) | no_return()
```

A function to call when decrypting any value. Takes the resource, field, records, and calculation context. Must return `:ok` or `{:error, error}`

# `cloak_options`

```elixir
@spec cloak_options(dsl_or_extended :: module() | map()) :: %{
  required(atom()) =&gt; any()
}
```

cloak DSL options

Returns a map containing the and any configured or default values.

# `cloak_vault`

```elixir
@spec cloak_vault(dsl_or_extended :: module() | map()) ::
  {:ok, module() | (any(), any() -&gt; any()) | mfa()} | :error
```

The vault to use to encrypt & decrypt the value. Accepts a module implementing `Cloak.Vault`, a `fun/2` of the form `(resource_module, context) -> vault_module`, or an MFA tuple. When a function or MFA is given, it is called at every encrypt and decrypt operation and its return value is used as the vault module.

# `cloak_vault!`

```elixir
@spec cloak_vault!(dsl_or_extended :: module() | map()) ::
  (module() | (any(), any() -&gt; any()) | mfa()) | no_return()
```

The vault to use to encrypt & decrypt the value. Accepts a module implementing `Cloak.Vault`, a `fun/2` of the form `(resource_module, context) -> vault_module`, or an MFA tuple. When a function or MFA is given, it is called at every encrypt and decrypt operation and its return value is used as the vault module.
